summary: Recce currently has ZERO coverage of STUN (3478/udp+tcp) or TURN/TURNS (5349/tls). Neither port appears in svcdetect.py's PORT_NAMES map (would render as "unknown"), nor in serviceenum.py's _NAME/_PORT script-router maps (so `recce services` prints no follow-up command), nor is there a per-service module under recce/services/. The intended shape is ntp.py: a UDP-first module with tiny stdlib-only packet builders, an analyze() aggregator invoked via svcprobe.iter_probe, findings() → svccommon.findings_to_vulns, plus wiring in cli/_service_helpers.py, cli/_phases.py, cli/_services.py, cli/parser.py (_add_t4), and webui/_common.py. STUN's value in an engagement is that its unauthenticated Binding request produces immediate protocol-level info disclosure (external IP mapping via XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS, server software via the SOFTWARE attribute), while TURN's unauthenticated Allocate deliberately answers 401 with REALM + NONCE attributes — a free correlation primitive that names the org's SIP/Kerberos/LDAP realm without any credentials. On top of that, misconfigured TURN servers are one of the highest-impact webRTC-era findings on the internet: open relays (Allocate without auth), long-term credentials sent cleartext on 3478 instead of 5349, and — worst — TURN allocations that will relay to RFC1918 or 169.254.169.254, turning the TURN server into a cloud-metadata SSRF pivot.

existing_coverage.notes: grep -riE 'stun|turn|3478|5349|webrtc' over recce/ returns zero substantive hits (only English word 'return' etc). Port 3478 absent from svcdetect.py:PORT_NAMES (nmap will report 'unknown' for firewalled listeners); ports 3478/5349 absent from serviceenum.py's _NAME table and _PORT fallback — `recce services` emits no follow-up command; no recce/services/stun.py or turn.py; no wiring in cli/_service_helpers.py, cli/_phases.py, cli/_services.py, cli/parser.py, webui/_common.py; no CVE entries for coturn/eturnal/restund in vuln/vulndb.py.

capabilities.name: port_map_registration
capabilities.description: Add 3478 → ('stun','STUN / TURN (unencrypted)'), 5349 → ('turns','STUN/TURN over TLS'), 5350 → ('nat-pmp-alt','NAT-PMP / STUN alt') to svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES so nmap-unknown UDP listeners get an inferred label with provenance=inferred. Add matching entries to serviceenum.py _NAME ('stun','turn','turns','stuns' → 'stun') and _PORT (3478,5349 → 'stun') so `recce services` recommends the follow-up script. Add parser _add_t4('stun', ...) tier-4 flag and wire cmd_stun in _phases.py.
capabilities.protocol_reference: IANA service registry: stun=3478/udp+tcp, stuns=5349/tcp, turn=3478, turns=5349

capabilities.name: stun_binding_probe
capabilities.description: Send an RFC 8489 §6 Binding Request (message type 0x0001, 20-byte header with magic cookie 0x2112A442 + random 96-bit transaction ID, zero attributes) to 3478/udp and 3478/tcp. A STUN server answers 0x0101 Binding Success with an XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS attribute (type 0x0020) carrying the client's public IP+port XORed with the magic cookie. Confirms STUN presence, measures round-trip, and yields the server's view of the scanner's NAT mapping — a pivot fact for cross-service correlation. Single 20-byte datagram, response 32-52 bytes.

capabilities.name: software_attribute_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Parse the SOFTWARE attribute (type 0x8022) from the Binding Response and TURN error responses. coturn (Citrix/CoTURN Inc), eturnal, restund, pion/webrtc-rs, Asterisk res_stun, aiortc all identify themselves with a free-form UTF-8 vendor+version string. Feed the extracted (product, version) tuple to parse_product_version() and the vulndb CVE mapper. Zero extra traffic beyond capability #2.

capabilities.name: turn_allocate_realm_nonce_disclosure
capabilities.description: Send an unauthenticated TURN Allocate request (message type 0x0003) with REQUESTED-TRANSPORT=17 (UDP, RFC 8656 §14.7). A conformant TURN server MUST answer 401 Unauthorized with an ERROR-CODE (0x0009), a REALM (0x0014), and a NONCE (0x0015) attribute. The REALM is a free credentialless leak of the deployment's identity namespace — it almost always matches the org's SIP domain / Kerberos realm / AD DNS domain / signaling-server hostname, so it feeds cross-service correlation to LDAP, Kerberos, SIP, SMTP and web modules. NONCE freshness + format also fingerprints server family (coturn nonces are hex; pion is base64).

capabilities.name: turn_open_relay_check
capabilities.description: After the 401 REALM+NONCE round-trip, retry Allocate with MESSAGE-INTEGRITY built from a well-known-empty username or missing credentials. Some misconfigured deployments (custom auth handlers, dev builds, older restund) return 0x0103 Allocate Success and hand out a RELAYED-ADDRESS (0x0016) with no auth. That is a wide-open relay: attackers get free egress bandwidth, source-IP laundering, and (via internal-address allocation, capability #7) an ingress path. Never actually use the relay; recce only records that the server accepted the allocation and immediately sends a Refresh with lifetime=0.

capabilities.name: cleartext_credential_channel
capabilities.description: If 3478 speaks TURN (Allocate answered 401 with REALM), record a finding: any client authenticating over 3478 sends the long-term-credential's HMAC-SHA1 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY, but the username, realm, nonce and the entire signaling payload traverse in cleartext — the server SHOULD offer 5349/tls (TURNS) instead. Cross-correlate: if 5349 is closed while 3478 is open + accepts credentials, this becomes high severity because there is no TLS fallback available at all.

capabilities.name: internal_address_relay_ssrf
capabilities.description: The single highest-impact TURN finding. Once a valid nonce is obtained (401 challenge alone is enough for the request format), send Allocate with a XOR-PEER-ADDRESS pointing at 169.254.169.254 (AWS/GCP/Azure IMDS), 127.0.0.1, or an RFC1918 address, then CreatePermission + Send toward it. A correctly configured TURN server MUST refuse per RFC 8656 §9 (`denied-peer-ip` in coturn config); a misconfigured one relays UDP into the internal network — turning TURN into a bidirectional SSRF/pivot with cloud-metadata reach. Recce sends the CreatePermission and one 0-byte Send indicator, never actual metadata queries; the finding is that the server accepted the permission for a forbidden peer.

capabilities.name: amplification_factor_measurement
capabilities.description: Compute response_bytes / request_bytes for the Binding Response (20-byte request → 32-52 byte response, ~2x) and the TURN 401 challenge (20-byte request → 80-120 byte response with REALM+NONCE+SOFTWARE, ~4-6x). Non-vulnerable by itself, but a >4x factor plus source-address-spoofable UDP is a reflective DDoS building block, and it slots into a future DDoS-posture aggregator alongside ntp monlist, memcached stats, and dns ANY.

capabilities.name: classic_stun_rfc3489_legacy
capabilities.description: Send a legacy RFC 3489 Binding Request (no magic cookie — first 4 bytes of transaction ID are random rather than 0x2112A442). A modern RFC 5389/8489 server MUST reject or ignore this; a legacy or backward-compatible daemon answers with MAPPED-ADDRESS (0x0001, plaintext IP+port, no XOR). Presence of ClassicSTUN indicates an outdated daemon, larger amplification surface, and often correlates with old coturn/vovida/stund builds carrying unpatched CVEs.

capabilities.name: nat_behavior_discovery_rfc5780
capabilities.description: Send Binding Requests with CHANGE-REQUEST (0x0003) flags set for change-IP and change-port, plus OTHER-ADDRESS (0x802C) probing. RFC 5780's diagnostic mode reveals whether the STUN server is dual-homed (many enterprise deployments are — the second address is often internal), the server's mapping/filtering behavior, and any secondary IP it will disclose in OTHER-ADDRESS. That second IP is a free host-discovery pivot — a second listener recce did not have to portscan for.

capabilities.name: turns_tls_posture
capabilities.description: On 5349/tcp complete a TLS handshake (reusing svccommon._tls_conn) and record: negotiated protocol version, cipher, certificate CN/SAN, issuer, notBefore/notAfter, and whether the server negotiates TLS 1.0/1.1 or exposes weak ciphers. TURNS certs frequently share SANs with the signaling WebSocket endpoint (wss://), which feeds the web/dns modules a hostname to enumerate. Also flag self-signed / expired / hostname-mismatched certs as usual.

capabilities.name: rest_api_ephemeral_credential_detection
capabilities.description: coturn / Janus / Jitsi / LiveKit deployments commonly use the RFC 7635 / draft-uberti-rtcweb-turn-rest style: usernames of the form '<expiry_epoch>:<user_id>' and passwords = base64(HMAC-SHA1(static-auth-secret, username)). Detect this by shape in captured usernames (regex `^\d{10,}:` in REALM/username fields observed via 401 responses or leaked config). Presence of this pattern is a signal to look for a REST endpoint on the paired signaling server that hands out credentials without authentication — a common WebRTC misconfig where /turn-credentials/ is world-readable.

capabilities.name: shared_secret_weakness_hint
capabilities.description: When credentials become available (either supplied via --creds, discovered by the REST endpoint from capability #12, or extracted from a captured WebRTC signaling exchange), the HMAC-SHA1 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY of any captured or generated Allocate can be cracked offline for the static-auth-secret with hashcat mode 31300 (or the shorter WebRTC-turn mode). Recce does not crack — it emits a runbook step + high-severity finding if the derived password is short (<12 chars) or matches known coturn defaults ('turnpassword', 'north', example.com samples).

capabilities.name: cve_lookup_for_detected_daemon
capabilities.description: Feed the (product, version) tuple extracted in capability #3 into vuln/vulndb.py — but the vulndb has zero coturn entries today, so this capability includes extending vulndb.py with the known-bad list: coturn <4.5.2 (CVE-2020-4067 loopback SSRF, CVE-2020-26262 IPv6 loopback bypass), coturn <4.5.0.7 (CVE-2018-4056 admin-listener PoW bypass), Cisco Meeting Server TURN CVEs, Asterisk res_stun_monitor bugs. Same shape as the mysql/openssh entries in vulndb.py.

capabilities.name: stun_tcp_transport_check
capabilities.description: STUN and TURN both run over TCP (RFC 6062 TURN-TCP, RFC 5389 §7.2.2) on the same 3478 port. Probe 3478/tcp with a Binding Request framed per RFC 4571 (2-byte length prefix). Presence indicates a fuller TURN deployment (webRTC clients use TCP TURN when UDP is blocked); absence of TCP support on a server that speaks UDP TURN is worth noting because it forces media over UDP (constrains firewall bypasses). Also enables TCP-relay allocation testing for the internal-address SSRF check in capability #7.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 6062 (TURN Extensions for TCP Allocations); RFC 4571 (framing)

cross_service_wire_candidates: External NAT mapping (XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS from capability #2) → feeds dns.py (reverse-cross-check against the discovered hostname's A record) and external.py (confirms which egress IP the target uses when it dials out, useful for pivoting and for correlating with any DNS answers from cloud metadata SSRF)

REALM value from TURN 401 (capability #4) → feeds ldap.py (bind DN heuristic — realm is usually the AD DNS domain), kerberos.py (Kerberos realm is upper-case of the STUN realm ~90% of the time), sip.py (SIP domain), smtp.py (HELO/EHLO domain), and web.py (co-hosted signaling server hostname). This is the single most valuable cross-service artifact — free identity-namespace disclosure without any auth.

SOFTWARE attribute product+version (capability #3) → feeds vuln/vulndb.py CVE mapping (same pipeline SSH/HTTP banners already use), and hints downstream modules — coturn implies Linux, Cisco Meeting Server implies Cisco infrastructure elsewhere

OTHER-ADDRESS second-listener IP (capability #10, RFC 5780) → feeds the host-discovery pipeline: a new IP recce never portscanned that is nonetheless known to be a live STUN server — schedule a full sweep of it

TURNS certificate CN + SAN list (capability #11) → feeds dns.py (subdomains to resolve), web.py (WebRTC signaling endpoints, typically wss://<same-host>/ or https://<same-host>/api/), and provides pivot hostnames for the whole webRTC platform

Detected REST-credential URL pattern (capability #12) → feeds web.py's URL wordlist: /turn-credentials, /api/turn, /_turn, /iceServers — often unauthenticated on the signaling server co-hosted with TURN
Amplification factor (capability #8) → feeds a future DDoS-posture cross-service report row alongside ntp monlist, dns ANY reflection, memcached stats, ssdp M-SEARCH

Internal-relay SSRF proof (capability #7) → feeds cloud-metadata / attack-path modules: if TURN relays to 169.254.169.254 it becomes an authenticated (over TURN) SSRF into IMDS, chainable with any cloud-role finding elsewhere
Long-term-credential MESSAGE-INTEGRITY captures (capability #13) → feeds hashcat handoff artifacts (mode 31300), parallel to the existing NTLM/kerberoast/asrep hash export flows

recommended_findings.title: TURN Allocate reveals authentication realm and nonce (unauthenticated realm disclosure)
TURN server accepts allocations without authentication (open relay)
TURN allocation permits relay to internal/loopback/cloud-metadata address (SSRF via TURN)
TURN long-term credentials accepted on cleartext 3478 with no TURNS (5349) alternative
STUN Binding Response discloses server software version via SOFTWARE attribute
STUN Binding Response reveals scanner's external IP mapping (informational — pivot fact)
STUN server responds to legacy RFC 3489 ClassicSTUN (outdated daemon, higher amplification)
STUN OTHER-ADDRESS attribute discloses a second server IP (undiscovered listener)
STUN/TURN reflective amplification factor exceeds 4x (DDoS building block)
TURNS (5349/tls) uses weak TLS version, weak cipher, or self-signed / expired certificate
TURN REST-style ephemeral-credential username pattern detected (co-hosted signaling API likely leaks credentials)
coturn <4.5.2 detected — CVE-2020-4067 loopback SSRF and related unauthenticated relay CVEs
TURN static-auth-secret is weak or matches a known default (offline HMAC-SHA1 crack)

implementation_notes: Create recce/services/stun.py modelled directly on ntp.py — same shape: is_stun(port) recognizer, _binding_request()/_allocate_request()/_change_request() bytes builders (stdlib struct only, no dependencies), _udp_exchange() (already generic enough to lift from ntp.py verbatim), probe(ip, port) returning a flat dict of booleans+values, findings(hosts, probes) building the finding dicts via svccommon.finding_builder, findings_to_vulns() delegating to svccommon.findings_to_vulns(fs, 'stun', 3478), and analyze() using svcprobe.iter_probe for budgeted concurrent execution with progress+state. For TURNS (5349/tls) reuse the TLS helper pattern from svcdetect._tls_conn / svccommon.https_conn — a TCP-STUN listener needs the RFC 4571 2-byte length framing, which is a 4-line difference from the UDP path. Wire the module into cli/_service_helpers.py (add 'stun': 'recce.services.stun'), cli/_phases.py (add ('stun','cmd_stun') tuple), cli/_services.py (add a cmd_stun following cmd_ntp exactly — module='stun', source='stun', label='STUN/TURN'), cli/parser.py (_add_t4('stun', 'STUN/TURN 3478,5349: TURN realm+nonce disclosure, open relays, internal-address SSRF, coturn CVEs, TURNS TLS posture')), and webui/_common.py (_cmd('STUN/TURN (realm disclosure + open relay + SSRF)', 'Services', 'optional')). Extend svcdetect.py PORT_NAMES with 3478/5349/5350 entries. Extend serviceenum.py _NAME with stun/stuns/turn/turns mapping to 'stun' and _PORT with 3478/5349. Extend vuln/vulndb.py with coturn CVE entries (CVE-2020-4067, CVE-2020-26262, CVE-2020-26263, CVE-2018-4056) using the existing product-lt schema. Runbook per target should include: nmap -sU -p3478,5349 --script stun-info,stun-version; a hand-crafted stun binding via `python3 -c` one-liner (offline-friendly since Kali has no bundled stun-client); openssl s_client -connect ip:5349 for TURNS cert; and a hashcat 31300 handoff line for any captured MESSAGE-INTEGRITY. All probes MUST be single-packet where possible (STUN is designed for that) and MUST refresh with lifetime=0 immediately after any successful Allocate to leave zero trace on the server. No third-party deps — stdlib socket + struct + ssl only, consistent with airgap constraint.
